name: 대륙 탐색
description: 지도가 화면을 채우고 국가·지형 선택은 작은 도구로 묶습니다.
prompt:
Create ONE polished high-fidelity 16:9 Korean game UI SCREENSHOT MOCKUP for the existing TownGrid game. This is an IMAGE DESIGN task, not code. Full bleed single screen, no presentation board, no device bezel, no comparison collage, no annotation arrows. Output large, crisp and legible.

REFERENCES: image 1 is the ACTUAL current world-selection screen, and is the factual reference for the isometric continent geography, recognizable pixel art style, green plains, snow mountain ranges, forests, narrow inland seas and national borders. Its DENSE UI is precisely what we are redesigning. Image 2 is the APPROVED minimalist in-game direction: flat dark teal #193f42, warm cream #fff7e8 text, ONLY the main CTA in muted vivid orange #ee701b, tiny radius 3px, simple line icons, contemporary readable Korean sans serif. Reuse this minimalist language. No rivets, metal bevels, ornamental frames, compartment boxes, dashboard charts, resource counters, gameplay toolbar, quest lists, or giant logo on this pregame screen. Use the actual world's recognizable isometric pixel landscape, not a generic fantasy painting or smooth 3D. The whole map is one large land continent occupying most of a rhombus, with narrow inland water under 20 percent; never an ocean with islands. Visual grouping by whitespace and a few flat dark teal surfaces. No sepia or parchment map. Restrained UI density and large map area. Crisp Korean typography.

GLOBAL UI shared across all three mockup states: top-left ONE slim flat teal bar with a simple left arrow and text "시작 지역"; center/top no huge banner. Top-right a compact outlined question mark icon only. The map fills the screen behind UI, on a muted sage-green ground. No frame enclosing the entire map. Small secondary controls are low-salience, with no unnecessary labels. Exactly one primary orange button if a primary action is needed. We want a quiet, game-first screen, not a marketing site.

STATE 1 — EXPLORE THE CONTINENT. The entire recognizable current continent should be shown generously across the screen, approximately centered, from a fixed isometric quarter view. Increase map occupation compared with actual screenshot by removing the ENTIRE right sidebar and all bottom legend cards. Preserve national border character: thin cream base with quiet nation-colored lines. Only five major readable map labels at overview level: "에스테른 왕국", "아르셀 연방", "네자르 마도국", "오르벨 왕국", and water label "유리 내해". Other small countries exist visually through subtle borders, not wall-to-wall labels. High mountains and forest clusters recognizable from reference, sparse small capital icons, broad empty land.
Beside top-left back bar place one restrained small flat teal dropdown reading "모든 국가⌄" and one reading "지형 찾기⌄". At lower center float ONLY a narrow dark teal pill-like rectangular strip reading "시작할 땅을 선택하세요" with a small pointer icon. This is an instruction, NOT a large CTA and NOT orange. Bottom-right one small shared teal control group with rotate-left, rotate-right, minus, plus icons, no individual boxed buttons. Screen has huge breathing space. No selected tile yet, no region details, no preview, no faction choices. Make the actual continent the hero and UI sparse.

name: 부지 선택

Bottom-right separate tiny zoom pair kept away from the central bar. Selected tile and map remain visually dominant.

name: 시작 전 확인
description: 빈 땅과 주변 지형을 크게 확인한 뒤 종족을 고르고 시작합니다.

Use natural pixel art with strong clean masses as in the approved second reference, slightly less saturated than that reference. Land connects into neighboring landscape beyond the outer border, no floating slab in space.

Left side small "에스테른 왕국" over bold "하벤 외곽 개척지", then one short muted line "비옥한 평야 · 24 × 24". Do not split humans/dwarves/titans into separate player factions, do not add employee hiring or big portraits. Right one orange large primary button "이 땅에서 시작 →". Tiny tertiary text link "자세히⌄" below the nation/site block can reveal details in implementation. No forced cinematic congratulations, no cards with stat lists, no resources and gameplay HUD, no technical words. Screen should feel calm and invite the player to build on this empty land.
